# Call Lark MCP server in remote mode (Deprecated)

Last updated on 2026-04-24

Lark Open Platform provides a remote MCP Server configuration feature that supports the Streamable HTTP transmission protocol, allowing users to securely and efficiently integrate and use rich Lark open capabilities in cloud scenarios with AI agents such as Cursor, Trae, Claude, and n8n via one-click integration.

## Configuring the MCP Server

Create a remote MCP service on the Lark MCP Configuration Platform and customize tools (i.e., Lark Open Platform server-side APIs) to flexibly build the MCP tools your business needs.

All tools are called via API under the identity of the currently logged-in user (user\_access\_token). Details:

* During the configuration process, the system guides you to complete the authorization operation for the logged-in user with one click. The MCP Server can only call tools on behalf of the user after authorization.
* The user\_access\_token itself has an expiry time. The remote MCP Server configuration feature supports automatic refreshing of the token before expiration.
* For more on user\_access\_token, see Obtaining user\_access\_token and Refreshing user\_access\_token.

1. Log in to the Lark MCP Configuration Platform.

   The remote MCP Server configuration function is in internal testing. If you cannot access the configuration platform, you can contact the customer success manager to activate the internal testing.
2. On the left side of the page, click **New MCP Service**.
3. On the service creation page, complete the following configurations.

   1. In the **MCP tool settings** area, confirm the current user identity.

      When using MCP to manage Lark business resources, the current displayed user will be used. Therefore, confirm the current user identity is correct; if not, log out and log back in with the correct user.
   2. In the **Add Tools** card, click **Add**.
   3. In the **Add tools** dialog, choose the needed tools.

      The platform provides **Ready-Made Toolkits** for selection. If none meet your needs, you can flexibly select various tools from the **Tailored Tools** list. For example, if your business needs MCP to manage Lark Multidimensional Tables, select Multidimensional Tables.

      Expand the tool list and click **Learn More** next to any tool to see detailed descriptions.
   4. Click **Add**, then in the pop-up **Get user authorization** dialog, confirm the authorization user login info and the permissions obtained by Lark MCP app, then click **Authorize**.
4. After successful addition, in the **How to use MCP server** area, select the **Transmission mode**, and view the **Server URL and JSON**.

   * The links included allow calling Lark tools as the currently logged-in user, effectively personal keys—do not disclose them to others.
   * The links have expiration; they become invalid after expiry. To extend, click **Reauthorize** below the URL/JSON.
   * If you suspect leakage, click **Reset Link** below the URL/JSON to invalidate the old link and generate a new one.

   * **Transmission mode**: Keep the default Streamable HTTP. Streamable HTTP is chunked streaming based on HTTP protocol and supports progressive transmission of any data format such as files and logs.
   * **Server URL and JSON**: Configure these links into your AI agents so they can remotely connect to Lark MCP services.

     Trae/Cursor support one-click installation; instructions follow in the next section. Other AI agents can set URL or JSON in their respective MCP configuration interfaces.

## One-click Installation to Trae/Cursor

After configuring the Lark MCP service, quick add entries for Trae and Cursor appear at the bottom of the service page for fast installation.

This approach requires Trae or Cursor installed locally.

Taking Trae as an example, the steps are:

1. Click **Cursor**, and follow prompts to open the Cursor client.
2. In the **MCP Tools** area, inside the **Install MCP Server?** card, click **Install**.

   After successful installation, the MCP Tools list will appear as shown below.

## Use MCP

Take Cursor as an example, to use Lark MCP services inside the AI agent.

1. Open a new chat session on the right side of the tool.

   * Select **Agent** at the bottom left.
   * Choose the large model as **Auto** or manually select any model (different models may have different outcomes).
2. Fill in your specific business requirements in the input box.

   This section provides the following example scenarios for your reference.

   1. Write prompt instructions so that the agent, based on a screenshot sample of a multi-dimensional table, uses Lark open API to batch read contents from cloud documents and extract the information into a multi-dimensional table, and finally drafts a technical solution document in Lark Docs.

      According to the cloud document link returned by the agent, access and view the document content.
   2. Continue writing prompt instructions to let the agent batch generate ten Lark cloud documents filled with simulated data, then generate the implementation code according to the above technical solution and ensure tests pass.

      The agent will first batch generate ten cloud documents.

      Sample document content:

      Then the agent will output corresponding project code for the technical solution.
   3. According to the test data requirements returned by the agent, submit the application’s App ID, App Secret, and the multi-dimensional table’s AppToken and TableId.

      You need to create an enterprise self-built application and multi-dimensional table resources for testing. Relevant operations refer to:

      Wait for the agent to complete testing and return results.
   4. Check the corresponding multi-dimensional table to confirm the test results are as expected.
   5. Apply the tested code inside the AI IDE.

## FAQ

### How to rename or delete a configured MCP Server?

1. Log in to the Lark MCP Configuration Platform.
2. In the left **Created MCP Services** list, select the service you want to operate.
3. In the title area, click **···**, then choose **Rename** or **Delete** for the current service.

### After configuring the tool, how to modify it? Is it necessary to regenerate the server URL after modification?

1. Log in to the Lark MCP Configuration Platform.
2. In the left **Created MCP Services** list, select the service you want to operate.
3. In the **MCP Tool Configuration** area, under **Add Tool** card, click **Edit**, modify the selected tool, and save.
4. After modification, refresh or restart the MCP service in the AI tool.

### What causes abnormal MCP Tools status display in Cursor?

* Symptom: After one-click installing MCP service to Cursor, the tool status indicator shows red.
* Reason: The status indicator may show red due to tool influence, generally not affecting MCP tool use.
* Solution: You can ignore this status, directly send requests in AI Chat, and judge based on AI response whether Lark MCP tool can be called normally. If usable, there is no problem. If not, reconfigure the remote MCP service and one-click install it to Cursor, then retry.

# Advanced configuration

Last updated on 2025-07-11

The contents of this article

The MCP tool supports a wide range of command parameters, allowing flexible configuration for suitable MCP startup commands. Detailed usage instructions for each parameter are provided below in **Parameter usage examples**.

## Prerequisites

The lark-mcp tool must be installed. Installation steps are as follows:

1. Run the following command in your local terminal to install lark-mcp.

   ```
   npm install @larksuiteoapi/lark-mcp -g
   ```

   If the terminal returns the message `It is likely you do not have the permissions to access this file as the current user`, you need to run the command as an administrator:`sudo npm install @larksuiteoapi/lark-mcp@beta -g`.
2. Run `lark-mcp -V` to check the MCP version.

   If the version is lower than 0.4.0, it is recommended to uninstall and reinstall lark-mcp:

   1. Uninstall lark-mcp: `npm uninstall @larksuiteoapi/lark-mcp -g`
   2. Reinstall lark-mcp: `npm install @larksuiteoapi/lark-mcp -g`
   3. Run `lark-mcp -V` again to verify the version information.
3. (Optional) Globally install OpenAPI MCP.

   There are two installation methods for the MCP tool: global installation and NPX installation. You can use either method to use the tool. Choose the installation method that suits your actual needs.

   * Global installation: installs to a global path (/usr/local/lib), commands are persistent, and system-level commands are available. Suitable for scenarios where command line tools are used frequently.
   * NPX installation: described in the Install and use OpenAPI MCP document. This method allows quick installation and use, but the command is not persistent as it is installed in the system's temporary cache, deleted after execution. Suitable for quick trials or one-time usage.

   After installing lark-mcp locally, you can use the MCP tool persistently (supported command parameters are referred to in the **Command Parameters** section below). Taking Trae as an example, the global installation steps are explained as follows:

   1. Complete the preparatory work.

      For details, see Install and use OpenAPI MCP.
   2. Open the Cursor tool.
   3. Open the terminal within the tool.
   4. Execute the following command to log in to OpenAPI MCP as a user:

      ```
      lark-mcp login -a <your_app_id> -s <your_app_secret>
      ```

      Here, `<your_app_id>` is the App ID of your Lark application, and `<your_app_secret>` is the App Secret of your Lark application. You can log in to the Lark Developer Console, and on the **Credentials & Basic Info** page of your created custom app details, obtain the **App ID** and **App Secret**.
   5. The terminal will display a URL for user authorization. You need to visit this URL within 60 seconds and complete the authorization.

      The authorization page looks like the image below. Ensure the user identity is as expected, and click **Authorize** so that the MCP tool can obtain the user access token (`user_access_token`).

      After successful authorization, the terminal will echo `success`.
   6. In the tool settings, select **Tools & Integrations > MCP Tools > Add Custom MCP**.
   7. Replace the default content with the following JSON and save:

      ```
      {



      "mcpServers": {



      "lark-mcp": {



      "command": "lark-mcp",



      "args": [



      "mcp",



      "-a",



      "<your_app_id>",



      "-s",



      "<your_app_secret>",



      "-d",



      "https://open.larksuite.com/",



      "--oauth"



      ]



      }



      }



      }
      ```

      Here, `<your_app_id>` is the App ID of your Lark application, and `<your_app_secret>` is the App Secret of your Lark application. You can log in to the Lark Developer Console, and on the **Credentials & Basic Info** page of your created custom app details, obtain the **App ID** and **App Secret**.
   8. After configuration, you need to disable and then re-enable lark-mcp.

      A properly running lark-mcp appears as shown below:

## Command parameter

### lark-mcp login

`lark-mcp login` is used to log in as a user and obtain the user identity credential (user\_access\_token). The supported command parameters are described in the table below.

| Parameter | Abbreviation | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--app-id` | `-a` | App ID of the Lark application. | `-a cli_xxxx` |
| `--app-secret` | `-s` | App Secret of the Lark application. | `-s xxxx` |
| `--domain` | `-d` | The API domain for Lark Open Platform, default is the Lark domain. | `-d https://open.larksuite.com` |
| `--host` | None | Listening host, defaults to localhost. | `--host 0.0.0.0` |
| `--port` | `-p` | Listening port, defaults to 3000. | `-p 3000` |
| `--scope` | None | Used to specify the API permissions for the user identity credential (user\_access\_token).   * Manually specified permissions must fall within the API permission scope that the application has applied for. For how to apply for application permissions, refer to Apply for API Permissions. * To enable automatic refreshing of user\_access\_token, the manually specified permissions must include the `offline_access` permission. For details, see Refresh user\_access\_token. * If the `--scope` parameter is not specified, the user is granted all API permissions the application has applied for by default. | `--scope offline_access doc:document` |

### lark-mcp logout

`lark-mcp logout` is used to log out a user and clear the user identity credential (user\_access\_token). The supported command parameters are described in the table below.

| Parameter | Abbreviation | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--app-id` | `-a` | App ID of the Lark application.   * If this parameter is not specified, user\_access\_tokens of all applications will be cleared. * If specified, only the user\_access\_token of the specified application will be cleared. | `-a cli_xxxx` |

### lark-mcp mcp

The supported command parameters of `lark-mcp mcp` are described in the table below.

| Parameter | Abbreviation | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--app-id` | `-a` | App ID of the Lark application. | `-a cli_xxxx` |
| `--app-secret` | `-s` | App Secret of the Lark application. | `-s xxxx` |
| `--domain` | `-d` | API domain of the Lark Open Platform, default is the Lark domain. | `-d https://open.larksuite.com` |
| `--tools` | `-t` | List of MCP tools that need to be enabled. Refer to tools and pass the corresponding **MCP tool names**.   * Support passing in preset toolsets. For example, if you pass in the preset toolset for messages and groups (preset.im.default), the specified range of message and group APIs will be enabled. For details on usage, see the below **Preset tool sets** section. * Supports passing in multiple items (including individual API tools and preset toolset names), separated by commas. * Fully covered, after running this parameter, only the API tools included in `-t` are available. | `-t im.v1.message.create,im.v1.chat.create` |
| `--tool-name-case` | `-c` | Format of the MCP tool registration name. Optional values are:   * snake (default) * camel * dot * kebab | `-c camel` |
| `--language` | `-l` | Tool language. Optional values are:   * zh: Chinese * en (default): English | `-l zh` |
| `--token-mode` | None | Specifies the Token type used when calling the API after the tool is started. The optional values are:   * auto (default value): Automatically selected by the large model inference. * tenant\_access\_token: Uses the application access token, and will filter out API tools that do not support tenant\_access\_token. * user\_access\_token: Uses the user access token, and will filter out API tools that do not support user\_access\_token. | `--token-mode auto` |
| `--user-access-token` | `-u` | User access token (user\_access\_token) for calling the API as a user. | `-u u-xxxx` |
| `--mode` | `-m` | Transmission mode. Optional values are:   * stdio (default) * sse * streamable | `-m sse` |
| `--oauth` | None | Configurable parameter for SSE/Streamable transmission mode, enabling automatic user identity login and authentication. | `lark-mcp mcp -m sse -a <your_app_id> -s <your_app_secret> --oauth` |
| `--host` | None | Listening host, default is localhost. | `--host 0.0.0.0` |
| `--port` | `-p` | Listening port, default is 3000. | `-p 3000` |
| `--version` | `-V` | Display version number. | `-V` |
| `--help` | `-h` | Display help information. | `-h` |

## Parameter usage examples

Parameters need to be configured in the MCP configuration file of the AI tool. For example, the MCP configuration file for the Cursor tool is mcp.json. The usage examples are shown in the table below.

| Usage | Example |
| --- | --- |
| Basic usage (using application identity) | Configure the App ID and App Secret of the application using `-a` and `-s`.   ```    {  "mcpServers": {  "lark-mcp": {  "command": "npx",  "args": [  "-y",  "@larksuiteoapi/lark-mcp",  "mcp",  "-a",  "<your_app_id>",  "-s",  "<your_app_secret>"  ]  }  }  } ``` |
| Specifies the Token type used when calling the API after the tool is started. | Specify the Token type through `--token-mode`. The permissible values are:   * auto (default value): Automatically selected by the large model inference. * tenant\_access\_token: Uses the application access token, and will filter out API tools that do not support tenant\_access\_token. * user\_access\_token: Uses the user access token, and will filter out API tools that do not support user\_access\_token.  ```    {  "mcpServers": {  "lark-mcp": {  "command": "npx",  "args": [  "-y",  "@larksuiteoapi/lark-mcp",  "mcp",  "-a",  "<your_app_id>",  "-s",  "<your_app_secret>",  "--token-mode",  "tenant_access_token"  ]  }  }  } ``` |
| Using user access token (user\_access\_token) | If you need to call the API as a specific user, you can specify the user access token (user\_access\_token) using `-u`.  Refer to FAQ for how to quickly obtain the user access token (user\_access\_token) corresponding to the application.   ```    {  "mcpServers": {  "lark-mcp": {  "command": "npx",  "args": [  "-y",  "@larksuiteoapi/lark-mcp",  "mcp",  "-a",  "<your_app_id>",  "-s",  "<your_app_secret>",  "-u",  "<your_user_access_token>"  ]  }  }  } ``` |
| Setting MCP tool language to Chinese | Specify the tool language using `-l`.  Setting the language to Chinese (zh) may consume more tokens. If you encounter token limit issues when integrating with the large model, consider using the default English (en).   ```    {  "mcpServers": {  "lark-mcp": {  "command": "npx",  "args": [  "-y",  "@larksuiteoapi/lark-mcp",  "mcp",  "-a",  "<your_app_id>",  "-s",  "<your_app_secret>",  "-l",  "zh"  ]  }  }  } ``` |
| Setting MCP tool name format to camel case | Set the tool name format using `-c`.  By setting the tool name format, the registered call name format of the tool in MCP can be changed. For example, the performance of `im.v1.message.create` in different formats:   * Snake case (default): `im_v1_message_create` * Camel case: `imV1MessageCreate` * Kebab case: `im-v1-message-create` * Dot case: `im.v1.message.create`   ```    {  "mcpServers": {  "lark-mcp": {  "command": "npx",  "args": [  "-y",  "@larksuiteoapi/lark-mcp",  "mcp",  "-a",  "<your_app_id>",  "-s",  "<your_app_secret>",  "-c",  "camel"  ]  }  }  } ``` |
| Specifying a custom domain | If you are using the international version of Lark or a custom domain, you can specify it using the `-d` parameter. Replace `<URL>` with the specific domain:   * The domain for the international version of Lark is: https://open.larksuite.com * Example of a custom domain: https://open.your-ka-domain.com  ```    {  "mcpServers": {  "lark-mcp": {  "command": "npx",  "args": [  "-y",  "@larksuiteoapi/lark-mcp",  "mcp",  "-a",  "<your_app_id>",  "-s",  "<your_app_secret>",  "-d",  "<URL>"  ]  }  }  } ``` |
| Setting the transmission mode | MCP tools support two transmission modes:   1. **stdio mode (default/recommended)**: `-m` value is `stdio`. This mode is suitable for integration with AI tools and communicates through standard input and output streams.      ```       {  "mcpServers": {  "lark-mcp": {  "command": "npx",  "args": [  "-y",  "@larksuiteoapi/lark-mcp",  "mcp",  "-a",  "<your_app_id>",  "-s",  "<your_app_secret>",  "-m",  "stdio"  ]  }  }  }    ``` 2. **SSE mode**: `-m` value is sse, providing an HTTP interface based on Server-Sent Events, suitable for web applications or scenarios requiring network interfaces.  After starting, the SSE endpoint can be accessed at `http://<host>:<port>/sse`.     1. Add the sse URL to the MCP configuration file and save the file.  As shown in the example URL below: `http://localhost:3000/sse`    2. Execute the following command in the terminal command line.         ```          lark-mcp mcp -a cli_xxxxxxx -s dfl4xxxx -m sse       ``` |
| Enable specific API tools | By default, the MCP service enables common APIs. To enable other tools or only specific APIs, you can specify them using the `-t` parameter.   * Refer to tools and pass the corresponding **MCP tool names**. * Supports passing in multiple items (including individual API tools and preset toolset names), separated by commas. * Support passing in preset toolsets. For example, if you pass in the preset toolset for messages and groups (preset.im.default), the specified range of message and group APIs will be enabled. For details on usage, see the below **Preset tool sets** section.   This method is a full override, and only the API tools included in `-t` will be enabled.   ```    {  "mcpServers": {  "lark-mcp": {  "command": "npx",  "args": [  "-y",  "@larksuiteoapi/lark-mcp",  "mcp",  "-a",  "<your_app_id>",  "-s",  "<your_app_secret>",  "-t",  "im.v1.message.create,im.v1.message.list,im.v1.chat.create"  ]  }  }  } ``` |
| Using environment variables instead of command-line parameters | ```    # Set environment variables  export APP_ID=<your_app_id>  export APP_SECRET=<your_app_secret>    # Start the service (no need to specify -a and -s parameters)  lark-mcp mcp ``` |

## Preset tool sets

| Toolset Name | Included APIs |
| --- | --- |
| preset.default | The default toolset enabled by OpenAPI MCP, includes:   * im.v1.chat.create: Create Chat Group * im.v1.chat.list: Get User or Bot Chat Groups * im.v1.chatMembers.get: Get Chat Members * im.v1.message.create: Send Message * im.v1.message.list: Get Chat History * bitable.v1.app.create: Create Bitable * bitable.v1.appTable.create: Create Table * bitable.v1.appTable.list: List Tables * bitable.v1.appTableField.list: List Fields * bitable.v1.appTableRecord.search: Search Records * bitable.v1.appTableRecord.create: Create Record * bitable.v1.appTableRecord.update: Update Record * docx.v1.document.rawContent: Get Document Raw Content * docx.builtin.import: Import documents, including three steps: uploading material/files, creating import tasks, and querying the results of import tasks. For details, see File Import Overview * docx.builtin.search: Search Cloud Documents * drive.v1.permissionMember.create: Add Collaboration Permission * wiki.v2.space.getNode: Get Knowledge Space Node * wiki.v1.node.search: Search Wiki * contact.v3.user.batchGetId: Get User ID by Phone or Email |
| preset.light | Concise set of API tools, including:   * im.v1.chat.search: Search the list of groups visible to the user or bot * im.v1.message.create: Send a message * im.v1.message.list: Get conversation history messages * bitable.v1.appTableRecord.search: Search records * bitable.v1.appTableRecord.batchCreate: Create multiple records * docx.v1.document.rawContent: Get the plain text content of the document * docx.builtin.import: Import documents, including three steps: uploading material/files, creating import tasks, and querying the results of import tasks. For details, see File Import Overview * docx.builtin.search: Search cloud documents * wiki.v2.space.getNode: Get knowledge space node information * contact.v3.user.batchGetId: Obtain user ID via mobile phone number or email |
| preset.im.default | Message and Chat Group API toolset, includes:   * im.v1.chat.create: Create Chat Group * im.v1.chat.list: Get User or Bot Chat Groups * im.v1.chatMembers.get: Get Chat Members * im.v1.chatMembers.create: Add Members to Chat * im.v1.message.create: Send Message * im.v1.message.list: Get Chat History |
| preset.base.default | Bitable API toolset, includes:   * bitable.v1.app.create: Create Bitable * bitable.v1.appTable.create: Create Table * bitable.v1.appTable.list: List Tables * bitable.v1.appTableField.list: List Fields * bitable.v1.appTableRecord.search: Search Records * bitable.v1.appTableRecord.create: Create Record * bitable.v1.appTableRecord.update: Update Record |
| preset.base.batch | Bitable Batch Processing API toolset, includes:   * bitable.v1.app.create: Create Bitable * bitable.v1.appTable.create: Create Table * bitable.v1.appTable.list: List Tables * bitable.v1.appTableField.list: List Fields * bitable.v1.appTableRecord.search: Search Records * bitable.v1.appTableRecord.batchCreate: Batch Create Records * bitable.v1.appTableRecord.batchUpdate：Update records |
| preset.doc.default | Cloud Document API toolset, includes:   * docx.v1.document.rawContent: Get Document Raw Content * docx.builtin.import: Import documents, including three steps: uploading material/files, creating import tasks, and querying the results of import tasks. For details, see File Import Overview * docx.builtin.search: Search Cloud Documents * drive.v1.permissionMember.create: Add Collaboration Permission * wiki.v2.space.getNode: Get Knowledge Space Node * wiki.v1.node.search: Search Wiki |
| preset.task.default | Task API toolset, includes:   * task.v2.task.create: Create Task * task.v2.task.patch: Update Task * task.v2.task.addMembers: Add Task Members * task.v2.task.addReminders: Add Task Reminders |
| preset.calendar.default | Calendar API toolset, includes:   * calendar.v4.calendarEvent.create: Create Calendar Event * calendar.v4.calendarEvent.patch: Update Calendar Event * calendar.v4.calendarEvent.get: Get Calendar Event * calendar.v4.freebusy.list: List Free/Busy * calendar.v4.calendar.primary: Get Primary Calendar |

# Develop OpenAPI MCP smart assistant

Last updated on 2025-10-14

This tutorial is based on the OpenAPI MCP tool, helping you quickly implement an OpenAPI MCP smart assistant Bot. This Bot can interact with users to call the OpenAPI MCP tool, completing automated tasks such as Lark Docs processing and calendar scheduling.

## Code sample

This tutorial provides sample code based on Node.js (MCP Larkbot Demo). You can visit GitHub to obtain the project.

## Supported capabilities

The smart assistant bot by default enables the APIs in the `preset.default` toolset. For details, refer to the preset toolset. Additionally, the Bot by default uses the **user identity** access token, meaning it will call the interface with the current **user identity**, thus filtering out API tools in the `preset.default` toolset that do not support `user_access_token`.

## Effect

The following example uses the claude-3.7-sonnet to demonstrate the effect of using the Bot Demo:

| Example | Create a Base and add specified columns | Get document content |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Requirement | Create a Base named "Project Tasks" with columns for "Task Name", "Responsible Person", and "Deadline". | Summarize the content of this document: https://www.feishu.cn/docx/EHumdbHVgoUMEixnAgOcQ2conXc |
| Effect |  |  |

## Preparations

Before starting the steps in this tutorial, you need to complete the following preparations:

* Have access to the AI model OpenAI API for configuring the `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_MODEL`, and `OPENAI_BASE_URL` parameters. This tutorial uses claude-3.7-sonnet as an example. To understand how to obtain the parameters, refer to Compatible with OpenAI API.
* Prepare a Node.js development environment for running the sample code based on Node.js. The environment requirements are as follows, and installation can be referred to Node.js.
  + Node.js version greater than or equal to v20.0.0
  + npm version greater than or equal to v8.0.0

## Procedure

This section introduces the overall steps for developing the MCP smart assistant Bot.

### Step 1: Create and configure the app

This step explains how to create an app and configure specified capabilities, permissions, and redirect URLs for the app. It is recommended that you create a new enterprise, create an app in the new enterprise, and add permissions to achieve permission exemption.

1. Log in to the Lark Developer console.
2. Click to create a **Custom App**, fill in the **Name** and **App Description**, and click **Create**.
3. Refer to the following table to configure the app.

| Configuration item | Steps | Illustration |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Add app capability: Bot | On the **App Capabilities > Add App Capability** page, add the **Bot** capability. |  |
| Apply for permissions:   * **App identity permissions**: Basic permissions for the app to send messages * **User identity permissions**: User identity permissions required by the API tools enabled by default in the OpenAPI MCP tool | 1. On the **Development Configuration** > **Permission Management** page, click the **Batch Import/Export Permissions** button. 2. In the pop-up window, paste the following permissions, then click **Next, Confirm New Permissions** > **Apply for Activation**.      ```       {  "scopes": {  "tenant": [  "im:message:send_as_bot",  "im:message:readonly",  "contact:user.id:readonly",  "im:message.group_at_msg:readonly",  "im:message.p2p_msg:readonly"  ],  "user": [  "im:chat:read",  "im:chat.members:read",  "im:message:readonly",  "wiki:wiki:readonly",  "docx:document:readonly",  "docx:document:create",  "search:docs:read",  "docs:document:import",  "docs:document.media:upload",  "docs:permission.member:create",  "base:app:create",  "base:table:create",  "base:table:read",  "base:field:read",  "base:record:retrieve",  "base:record:create",  "base:record:update",  "contact:user.id:readonly"  ]  }  }    ```      If the **user permissions** you want to activate are not exactly the same as the following permissions, you need to modify the OAuth authorization scope configuration in the sample code `nodejs\src\config\index.ts` file to ensure that the activated **user permissions** are consistent with the OAuth authorization scope in the code. Otherwise, the user permissions activated here will be invalid due to authentication failure. |  |
| **Security Settings - Redirect URL** | 1. Click **Security Settings** in the left navigation bar. 2. In the **Redirect URL** section, enter the following URL and click **Add**.     ```    http://localhost:3000/callback    ``` |  |

### Step 2: Download the sample code and configure the `.env` file

1. Click the link here to download the Node.js sample code and navigate to the `nodejs` folder. You can also use the Git command to clone the GitHub project:

   ```
   git clone https://github.com/larksuite/lark-samples



   cd mcp_larkbot_demo/nodejs
   ```
2. Inside the `nodejs` folder, create a file named `.env` and paste and configure the following environment variables. You can also directly modify and rename the existing `.env.example` file to `.env`. A configuration example is shown below:

   ```
   # App configuration example



   APP_ID=cli_a8f75e4d91****** # The App ID of the app you created



   APP_SECRET=RekOQ8EV14shNMtZokRAmdmlab****** # The App Secret of the app you created



   LARK_DOMAIN=https://open.larksuite.com  # Lark domain, keep unchanged



   # Choose one of the following OpenAI API configurations



   # Remote Ark configuration example



   OPENAI_API_KEY=jgzRNvqN526pkr5IlZ3iXLTs********_GPT_AK



   OPENAI_MODEL=gcp-claude37-sonnet



   OPENAI_BASE_URL=https://search-va.byteintl.net/gpt/openapi/online/v2/crawl/openai/deployments



   # Local Ollama configuration example



   OPENAI_API_KEY=your_openai_api_key # Ollama does not validate this



   OPENAI_MODEL=qwen2:7b



   OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434/v1



   # Server configuration



   PORT=3000     # Server configuration, can remain unchanged
   ```

### Step 3: Install dependencies and start the project

1. Navigate to the `nodejs` folder and install the project dependencies:

   ```
   npm install
   ```
2. Start the service:

   ```
   npm run dev:webhook
   ```

   The successful startup output is shown below:

### Step 4: Add events

After successfully starting the project and establishing a long connection in the previous step, you can configure the event subscription method and add events in the Developer console. In this tutorial, you need to add the Receive Message event (`im.message.receive_v1`) for the app. The steps are as follows:

1. On the **Development Configuration > Events & Callbacks > Event Configuration** page, edit the **Subscription mode**.
2. Select **Send notifications to developer's server**，enter a URL to subscribe to events, and click **Save**.

The Lark platform cannot access your local service directly. You will need to expose it via a publicly accessible URL.

3. In the **Added Events** section, click **Add Event** and add the **Receive Message** event.

### Step 5: Publish the app

The app must be published for the configurations to take effect. The publishing steps are as follows:

1. On the app's **Version Management & Release** page, click **Create Version**.
2. On the **Version Details** page, configure the following app information and click **Save**:

   1. **App Version Number**: A custom version number displayed to users. For the first release, you can set a version number such as `1.0.0`. Subsequent iteration version numbers must be higher than the previous one.
   2. **Update Notes**: Details of the current app update, which will be displayed in the app's update log.
   3. **App Capabilities**, **Permission Changes**: Review and ensure that the changes meet expectations.
   4. **Available Scope**: The app's available scope. Click **Edit** to manually adjust this scope.
   5. **Reason for Application**: A custom reason for publishing the app, which will be reviewed by the approver.
3. In the pop-up dialog, click **Confirm Release**.
4. The enterprise administrator will receive a notification. Once approved, the app will be successfully published. You can also create a new enterprise, create an app within the new enterprise, and add permissions to achieve permission-free approval.

## Experience the demo

After the app is published and the project is started, you can open the intelligent assistant Bot in the Lark client and interact with the Bot to experience the Demo.

1. Search for the created app in the Lark client and send a message. For example: `Find any wiki docs whose title contains "mcp"`.
2. After the service is started and the first message is received, the Bot will send an authorization login link. Click the link and complete the authorization on the page.
3. After obtaining user authorization, the bot will automatically call the tool to search for relevant documentation for you.
4. You can continue the conversation by entering other requests, and the bot app will automatically call the corresponding tools to fulfill them. For example:

   * Example 1: `Sumarize the scenarios and benefits of remote mode`
   * Example 2: `How to enable this MCP remote mode feature`
5. To clear the context of the current conversation, enter the `/clear` command.

## FAQs

### Authorization fails when clicking the user authorization login link?

When interacting with the Bot, if the authorization link sent by the Bot does not display the following successful login page, please follow these steps to troubleshoot:

* Ensure that the `APP_ID` and `APP_SECRET` in the `.env` file are correctly configured.
* Confirm that the redirect URL configured in the Developer console is `http://localhost:3000/callback`.
* Ensure that only one service is running at a time:
  + For Windows users, you can check processes in **Task Manager**.
  + For macOS/Linux users, you can check processes in **Activity Monitor** or use the `ps aux` command.
* Restart your computer and try again.

### Still prompted with insufficient permissions after enabling permissions in the developer console?

Please follow these steps to troubleshoot:

1. Ensure that the app has been published after enabling permissions in the Developer console. A published app will display "All current changes have been published".
2. In the sample code, locate the `mcp_larkbot_demo/nodejs/src/config/index.ts` file, specifically the **OAuth Authorization Scope** section. Ensure that the permissions here match the **User Permissions** enabled in the Developer console. Otherwise, the enabled user permissions will be invalid due to authorization failure.
3. After modifying the sample code, stop the service, restart it, and authorize again.

### How to add more capabilities to the Bot Demo/How to enable custom toolset?

The Bot Demo by default enables the APIs in the `preset.default` toolset. For details, refer to the preset toolset. Additionally, the Demo uses the user identity access token by default, meaning it will call the APIs with the current user's identity, thus filtering out the API tools in the `preset.default` toolset that do not support `user_access_token`.

To customize tools or toolsets, follow these steps:

1. Go to the `nodejs\src\service\mcp.ts` file, and at line 53, modify the code as per the comments to customize tools or toolsets. The following example sets the toolset to the calendar API toolset. Refer to the preset toolset to understand the supported APIs.

   * Refer to tools to pass the **MCP tool name** corresponding to the tool.
     + Refer to the preset toolset to pass the preset toolset name.
     + Multiple parameter values (including individual API tools and preset toolset names) can be passed simultaneously, separated by commas.
     + This method is a full overwrite, meaning it will overwrite the default enabled API tools and only enable the API tools included in `-t`.

   ```
   let args = [



   '-y',



   '@larksuiteoapi/lark-mcp',



   'mcp',



   '-a',



   config.lark.appId,



   '-s',



   config.lark.appSecret,



   '-d',



   config.lark.domain,



   '-t',   // MCP tool or toolset to be enabled



   'preset.calendar.default', // Add the preset calendar API toolset here. It will overwrite the default enabled API tools and only enable the API tools included in `-t`



   ];
   ```
2. Based on the enabled tools and toolsets, go to the corresponding API documentation to understand the permissions that need to be enabled. For example, for the `preset.calendar.default` toolset, the included interfaces are:

   * calendar.v4.calendarEvent.create: Create calendar event
   * calendar.v4.calendarEvent.patch: Update calendar event
   * calendar.v4.calendarEvent.get: Get calendar event
   * calendar.v4.freebusy.list: Query free/busy information of the primary calendar
   * calendar.v4.calendar.primary: Query primary calendar information
3. By reviewing the API documentation, the permissions that need to be enabled are:

   ```
   calendar:calendar;calendar:calendar:read
   ```
4. Go to the Developer console to enable application and user identity permissions for the app, and publish the app:
5. In the sample code, locate the "OAuth authorization scope" in the `mcp_larkbot_demo/nodejs/src/config/index.ts` file, and add the `calendar:calendar;calendar:calendar:read` permissions.
6. Restart the service. After completing user authorization, interact with the Bot to verify the effect.

# OpenAPI MCP overview

Last updated on 2025-06-30

The contents of this article

OpenAPI MCP Tool (hereinafter referred to as "MCP Tool") can help you quickly integrate AI agents with Lark's open capabilities, enabling automated scenarios such as document processing, conversation management, and calendar scheduling based on agents.

## Features

The MCP Tool uses the MCP (Model Context Protocol) protocol to connect with the Lark Open Platform, providing a rich set of OpenAPI tools that cover Lark's core functions (such as messages, groups, calendars, Base apps, etc.). It also supports application access tokens (tenant\_access\_token) and user access tokens (user\_access\_token) to ensure secure and controllable API calls. The features of the MCP Tool are as follows:

* Provides a simple and easy-to-use command line interface for quick configuration and startup.
* Supports various configuration methods, adapting to different usage scenarios.
* Seamlessly integrates with mainstream AI tools (such as Trae, Cursor, Claude).
* After configuring the application information, the application access credentials can be obtained automatically; after logging into the MCP and completing user authentication, the user access credentials can be obtained automatically, with support for automatic refresh.

## Typical use cases

AI will plan based on the actual input prompt and invoke different OpenAPIs, so the permissions that the application needs to open may vary.

| Scenario Example | Pre-Configuration | Trae Running Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Initialize Project Management Base apps | * **Application Capability**: Bot * **Application Permissions**:  View, comment, edit and manage Base apps |  |
| Create Group Chat, Add Members and Send Lark Card | * **Application Capability**: Bot * **Application Permissions**:  Retrieve and update group information  Send messages as an application * **Others**: Ensure all members in the group are within the application's visibility scope. Refer to Configure Application Availability. |  |
| Summarize Group Messages and Record in Base apps | * **Application Capability**: Bot * **Application Permissions**:  Retrieve all messages in the group (sensitive permission)  Create Base apps  Add new data tables  Add new records * **Others**: Bot is in the group chat |  |
| Grant Base apps Permissions to Group Members | * **Application Capability**: Enable bot capability * **Application Permissions**:  View group members  View, comment, edit and manage Base apps * **Others**: Bot in group chat; Bot has management permissions for the Base apps |  |

## Supported openAPI

You can check tools to get the list of OpenAPI supported by the MCP Tool on the Lark Open Platform. You can also determine if an API is supported within the MCP Tool through the API documentation. For example, open an API development document, such as Send Message. If there is a **"Try it out"** button, it indicates that the API is available within the MCP Tool.

* APIs in grayscale (i.e., APIs marked as **Limited access** at the beginning of the API documentation) are temporarily not supported in the MCP tool.
* APIs related to image or file upload/download are temporarily not supported within the MCP tool.

## MCP tool naming scheme

The MCP Tool follows the naming scheme of `biz.version.resource.method`, consistent with the method naming of the server-side Node SDK. You can obtain the name of an OpenAPI in the MCP Tool in the following way:

In the API documentation, click **Try it out** and check the **Node SDK** sample code. The function after the `client` method is the name of the API in the MCP Tool. For example, as shown in the figure below, the name of the Send Message API is `im.v1.message.create`.

# Create a Lark agent app in one click

Last updated on 2026-06-17

Lark Open Platform provides a **one-click way to create a Lark agent app**. This helps AI agents such as OpenClaw and Hermes connect to Lark quickly and interact with users inside Lark.

## When to use

You can use this when you have built an AI agent, such as one based on OpenClaw or Hermes, and want to bring it into Lark so it can interact with users there. This includes sending and receiving messages, transferring files, and handling other common interactions.

In the traditional setup flow, users need to go to the Lark developer console, create an app manually, and then configure permissions and event subscriptions. This can take time and adds unnecessary setup work.

With this SDK, an AI agent can help users create a Lark app in one step. The SDK automatically preconfigures all required permissions and event subscriptions (see the Appendix). The user only needs to scan a code and confirm. After that, the App ID and App Secret are returned and the app is ready to use.

## What you get

After you integrate the SDK, users create a Lark app in three steps:

**Step 1: The user opens the app creation link or scans the QR code**

Example link:

```
https://open.larksuite.com/page/launcher?user_code=XXXX-XXXX&from=sdk&source=node-sdk&tp=sdk
```

> The link is valid for 10 minutes and can only be used once by a single user via click or scan.

**Step 2: Create an app. You can select an existing app or create a new one**

You can use SDK parameters to pass the app avatar, name, and description.

**Step 3: Finish creation and get credentials**

Get the App ID and App Secret automatically after the app is created. Use them right away to call Lark APIs—this flow already sets up all required scopes and event subscriptions.

## Integration

## Appendix: agent app configuration checklist

Use the default scopes and event subscriptions below. This preset covers common AI Agent scenarios, including:

* Receive and send messages in 1:1 chats and group chats.
* @mention the Agent in document comments so the Agent can reply to the comment thread.

### App capabilities (Feature)

Bot

### Permission management

* **App identity scopes**

| Scope name | Scope key |
| --- | --- |
| Manage the app’s own resources | application:application:self\_manage |
| Create, update, and delete the bot menu | application:bot.menu:write |
| Read card data | cardkit:card:read |
| Create and update cards | cardkit:card:write |
| Read basic directory information | contact:contact.base:readonly |
| Add and reply to comments in Docs | docs:document.comment:create |
| Delete comments in cloud docs | docs:document.comment:delete |
| Read comments in cloud docs | docs:document.comment:read |
| Update comments in cloud docs | docs:document.comment:update |
| Reply to, update, and delete comments in cloud docs | docs:document.comment:write\_only |
| Convert text to doc blocks | docx:document.block:convert |
| Read new Docs | docx:document:readonly |
| Edit new Docs | docx:document:write\_only |
| Read file metadata in Drive | drive:drive.metadata:readonly |
| Subscribe to bot added/removed events in chats | im:chat.members:bot\_access |
| Read chat information | im:chat:read |
| Update chat information | im:chat:update |
| Create group | im:chat:create |
| Read group messages where other bots and users @mention the current bot | im:message.group\_at\_msg.include\_bot:readonly |
| Read group messages where users @mention the bot | im:message.group\_at\_msg:readonly |
| Read 1:1 messages sent to the bot | im:message.p2p\_msg:readonly |
| Read pinned messages | im:message.pins:read |
| Pin and unpin messages | im:message.pins:write\_only |
| Read message reactions | im:message.reactions:read |
| Add and delete message reactions | im:message.reactions:write\_only |
| Read 1:1 and group chat messages | im:message:readonly |
| Send messages as the app | im:message:send\_as\_bot |
| Send messages to multiple users in batch | im:message:send\_multi\_users |
| Send system messages based on specific templates | im:message:send\_sys\_msg |
| Update messages | im:message:update |
| Upload and fetch image/file resources | im:resource |
| Get bot basic information | application:bot.basic\_info:read |
| View wiki space node information | wiki:node:read |
| Read slash command | application:app\_slash\_command:read |
| Edit slash command | application:app\_slash\_command:write |

* **User identity scopes**

| Scope name | Scope key |
| --- | --- |
| Access authorized data continuously | offline\_access |

* **Reference: scope import list for the Developer Console**

```
{



"scopes": {



"tenant": [



"contact:contact.base:readonly",



"im:chat:create",



"im:chat:read",



"im:chat:update",



"im:message.group_at_msg:readonly",



"im:message.p2p_msg:readonly",
```
